title: HorizonAI - POC scoping: capacity & autoscale
summary: POC scoping to define capacity sizing and autoscaling for a 4-week pilot. Customer wants reserved baseline GPUs with burst pool and clear fallback policies. Key success criteria: 95th pct latency <250ms for chat workloads, cost below $0.0008/token, and reproducible benchmark run on sample traffic.
header:
Date: 2025-04-25 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Ana Gomez (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (HorizonAI CTO), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Jamal Brooks (Infra), Maya Singh (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Michael Chen: alright thanks everyone for joining, we have a packed agenda to nail down the POC sizing and autoscale plan. uh quick intro round?
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, CTO at Horizon. we'll mostly be driving infra decisions, priya will handle ml workload details.
[00:18] Priya Rao: hey all, priya, ML eng. our main thing is chat assistant workload, average seq len 256, heavy burst during support hours.
[00:29] Jamal Brooks: jamal, infra. we need clear reserved capacity and burst model, also must fit our VPC constraints.
[00:36] Michael Chen: perfect. Sofia, quick walk-through of what Redwood suggests for POC?
[00:40] Sofia Patel: yeah so typical POC flows: baseline reserved GPUs to match 95th pct load, a burst pool for traffic spikes, and fallback policies — e.g. downshift to smaller quantized model or route to hosted lower-tier nodes if reserved are saturated. we recommend an initial baseline that covers your steady qps and a 2x burst buffer.
[01:02] Priya Rao: to give numbers: at peak we see roughly 60 concurrent chats, avg QPS ~20, but spikes up to 120 qps for short windows. 256 tokens avg but some go to 1k.
[01:18] Ana Gomez: good to call out tail sequences — long requests will inflate GPU mem usage and reduce throughput. did you capture quantization constraints?
[01:25] Priya Rao: we're fine with 4-bit quantized weights for latency, but want to check quality regression.
[01:31] Michael Chen: great. Jamal, any infra red lines?
[01:34] Jamal Brooks: SOC2 is required, SAML SSO, KMS for encryption — but specifically for POC we need to avoid customer data leaving our VPC unless sandboxed. can we do private POC?
[01:44] Sofia Patel: yes, Redwood Private option supports VPC peering and on-prem hooks. for short POC we can deploy a private tenant in your cloud region — we'll need a service account and a few network rules.
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: timeline? we want benchmarks next week ideally. is that feasible?
[02:00] Michael Chen: probably — depends on sample data and permissions. typical timeline we propose: week 0: infra set up and sample ingestion, week 1: baseline runs, week 2: stress/burst runs and fallback validation, week 3: tuning and final benchmarks. 3-4 weeks total.
[02:18] Priya Rao: we can provide anonymized traffic traces and a 500-request test set by Monday.
[02:24] Michael Chen: ok that helps. let's talk capacity math real quick — Sofia?
[02:28] Sofia Patel: sure. given 20 steady qps and 120 peak, and model perf targets, we size baseline to handle steady plus moderate spike. e.g., if an A100 80GB can handle approx 30 concurrent chat sessions at 256 tokens depending on model, we'd start with 2 reserved A100s (baseline ~60 concurrent). then configure burst pool of additional 4 GPUs to absorb spikes up to 180 concurrent. that's a 2 baseline / 4 burst split.
[02:56] Priya Rao: what's the latency numbers on that?
[02:58] Sofia Patel: depends on model. for an LLaMA-variant 7B quantized on A100 we typically see p50 ~60-80ms, p95 ~180-250ms under steady load. with burst autoscale there's transition overhead ~1-2s for new instances join, so we use warm standby and fast provisioning.
[03:18] Jamal Brooks: warm standby meaning reserved burst nodes pre-warmed? that has cost impact.
[03:23] Ana Gomez: yes — two strategies: pre-warm a small warm pool (idling but GPU allocated) or rely on fast cold start with request queueing + model fallback. for POC we often recommend 1-2 warm nodes to keep tail latency acceptable without huge cost.
[03:37] Michael Chen: and fallback paths — prioritize which?
[03:39] Sofia Patel: fallback order we typically configure: 1) route to smaller quantized model on same GPU (e.g., 7B -> 3B), 2) route to hosted multi-tenant nodes (cheaper but higher latency), 3) degrade to cached responses for repeat prompts. we can make per-route policies.
[03:56] Priya Rao: how do we validate quality when falling back? automatic A/B sampling?
[04:00] Ana Gomez: yes, Redwood Console can do shadowing and sample scoring. you can set regression thresholds — if fallback responses exceed delta on eval set, we can alert and auto-failover back to reserved.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: cost question — what cost impact of 2 reserved + 4 burst with 1 warm node?
[04:17] Michael Chen: rough back-of-envelope: reserved baseline committed monthly alters pricing — for POC we'll give short-term reserved pricing. ballpark for cloud GPUs plus Redwood runtime is about $X/hour per A100 for reserved vs $Y/hour for burst; we'll send exact numbers in pricing doc. target cost per token they mentioned $0.0008 — we'll test to ensure close.
[04:35] Priya Rao: benchmark specifics: we want p95 latency <250ms for chat, throughput >=20 qps sustained, and cost per 1M tokens below $800. also reproducibility: same run should produce near-identical latencies within 5%.
[04:53] Sofia Patel: agreed. we'll provide a benchmark harness (script + metrics) and run on your sample traces. can you provide typical prompt length distribution?
[04:59] Priya Rao: yes, median 120 tokens, 75% under 400, tail to 2k in 2% of requests.
[05:08] Ana Gomez: tail will need special handling: we can set a policy to offload >1024 token requests to isolated nodes to protect baseline throughput.
[05:15] Jamal Brooks: what's the autoscale cooldown and scale unit? we worry about thrash with chat spikes.
[05:20] Sofia Patel: default cooldown 60s, scale in 5m to avoid thrash; scale unit is by GPU pod. we can set smaller units if using fractional GPU sharing but for POC we usually do whole GPUs.
[05:30] Michael Chen: are there any compliance hurdles for private POC? Liam?
[05:34] Liam O'Connor: KMS + audit logs are musts; need to keep logs for 90d. also need RBAC for team members.
[05:40] Sofia Patel: Redwood Private supports KMS integration and audit logging; we will share SOC2 docs and a checklist.
[05:45] Priya Rao: bench run — can Redwood run both latency and quality eval simultaneously?
[05:50] Ana Gomez: yes, the harness does latency, throughput, and quality scoring using your eval set; we can run isolated and mixed workloads to simulate production.
[05:58] Priya Rao: for baselining the POC, what metrics we put on the table as success criteria?
[06:02] Michael Chen: let's propose the POC success criteria as: 1) p95 latency <= 250ms for <=1024 token requests under defined load, 2) throughput >= 20 qps sustained during a 10-min window, 3) cost per 1M tokens <= $800, 4) Passing security checklist (KMS, SSO, audit logs), 5) runbook for fallback validated with <2% error rate on fallback responses.
[06:26] Maya Singh: timeline recap?
[06:28] Michael Chen: week 0 (this week): share traces & credentials; week 1: infra + baseline runs; week 2: burst/stress + fallback tests; week 3: tuning + final benchmark and handoff. if all good, discuss Dedicated sizing and contract.
[06:41] Jamal Brooks: we will need a network diagram for the private deployment.
[06:44] Ana Gomez: we'll attach a sample diagram and network rule list.
[06:47] Liam O'Connor: one more question — can we request H100s instead of A100s?
[06:51] Sofia Patel: yes, H100s give better perf for large models but cost more. for 7B family A100 is good; if you want to run 13B+ or full-context long sequences H100 is recommended. we can size both variants in the POC.
[07:06] Priya Rao: ok let's run baseline on A100 and a small H100 run for comparison.
[07:10] Michael Chen: great. any other blockers?
[07:13] Maya Singh: pricing doc and security pack need to go to procurement.
[07:16] Michael Chen: we'll send both. Also we'll request a short SLA doc for the POC.
[07:21] Ana Gomez: note: we'll include a benchmark spreadsheet link — /redwood/benchmarks/horizonai.xlsx — with expected metrics and CSV of sample traces.
[07:30] Priya Rao: thanks, appreciate it.
[07:33] Michael Chen: OK recap of next steps and owners.
[07:36] Sofia Patel: recap now?
[07:37] Michael Chen: yes.
[07:38] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
